Can you send:

High-level next steps (shortest path):
1) You complete the vendor intake + return W-9/tax entity details.
2) Finance verifies tax entity and issues vendor ID (48–72 hours typical once we have completed intake).
3) Marketplace-specific enablement (parallel):
   - AWS: we provide our AWS Partner ID and SaaS listing requirements; procurement can attach PO to our AWS listing once vendor ID exists.
   - Azure: transactable listing requires MPN ID and an invoice/billing contact — we’ll supply partner and offer IDs.
   - GCP: we accept POs directly to invoices@redwood.ai and provide license keys/consumption reporting for reconciliation.

Regarding payment terms: we typically standardize on Net30. Net45 can be considered but requires a finance approval and a signed exception (Vanessa — can you confirm). If you want to proceed with a preliminary PO for internal routing, we accept that as long as it’s marked as preliminary and references the HubSpot deal id (we’ll provide on confirmation).

Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow to align on the paperwork and whether FastRetail needs the sponsor agreement routed via DocuSign? Here’s a Calendly: https://calendly.com/evelyn-redwood/marketplace-onboarding

Best,
Evelyn Hart

Hi Alexa — Vanessa from Finance here. Thanks for the PO and the context. Confirming the operational path and the documents we need from FastRetail to complete vendor creation and enable marketplace procurement flows.

Required items from FastRetail (please return in a single email if possible):
- Completed vendor intake form (vendor_intake_form_redwood.pdf)
- Signed W-9 (or equivalent tax form) and legal billing entity name
- Copy of preliminary PO (you already shared FR_PO_12345.pdf — good)
- Primary invoice recipient email and purchase order contact

Cloud marketplace specifics (how we handle the PO routing once vendor is created):
- AWS Marketplace (SaaS):
  - We provide our AWS Partner ID and Offer ID after vendor creation.
  - PO routing: procurement attaches the PO to the AWS subscription/offer; billing reconciled via AWS billing unless you request direct invoicing.
  - Common exception: Net45 is allowed on a case-by-case basis; it requires a signed payment exception form and approval by Finance. If FastRetail requires Net45, please indicate the fiscal reason and include an approver contact.

- Azure Marketplace (transactable listing):
  - Requires MPN ID + Offer publishing. We can accept the PO; final invoicing typically flows through Microsoft unless you request direct billing.
  - Azure transactable listings require Publisher/Offer IDs — we will share those once listing is associated to FastRetail’s procurement record.

- GCP Marketplace / Direct billing:
  - We accept POs directly to invoices@redwood.ai. Provide the PO number and billing contact and we’ll issue an invoice against that PO.
  - For consumption-based products, we provide monthly usage reconciliations and a license key if applicable.

Administrative notes:
- To approve Net45 we need a named approver and a business justification; lead time for approval is ~3 business days.
- Once we have the completed intake and W-9, Finance will create the vendor ID and share the HubSpot vendor record and Redwood vendor number.
- DocuSign sponsor/vendor agreement link: https://app.docusign.com/FR-Redwood-SponsorAgreement — please sign and return.

Attachments included from our side: vendor_intake_form_redwood.pdf; marketplace_onboarding_checklist.xlsx; redwood_w9_signed.pdf

If you’re good with the list, we’ll move vendor creation to priority and provide our partner IDs within 48 hours of receiving the intake + W-9.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
